title: Coursiv vs Learnova: which AI learning app is worth it in 2026?
lede: The two most-advertised AI learning apps, compared honestly, plus a third option if neither fits how you learn.
keyTakeaways: Coursiv and Learnova are more alike than their ads suggest: both are course-style apps that teach AI tools in short, guided daily lessons.
The formats differ: Coursiv leans on a 28-day challenge format, while Learnova is a tiered course library with quizzes and a practice playground.
Pricing is where people get caught: check what any intro offer renews at before subscribing.
If lessons feel like homework you never finish, the real answer may be neither: practice-first apps like Iro AI build the habit instead.
description: An honest Coursiv vs Learnova comparison for 2026: how the two AI learning apps differ on teaching style, pricing, and free access, plus a third option if neither fits how you learn.

sections.heading: What they have in common
sections.html:
Coursiv and Learnova compete for the same person: someone who has heard they should "learn AI," wants a structured, beginner-friendly way to do it on their phone, and found both apps through ads. The overlap is real: both teach tools like ChatGPT through short, guided lessons; both are mobile-first; both use quizzes to check understanding; and both monetize through subscriptions.

Because of that overlap, the choice between them comes down to format details and pricing mechanics rather than radically different products. Here is the honest breakdown.

sections.heading: Where Coursiv wins
sections.html: Coursiv's strength is momentum. The 28-day challenge framing gives beginners a clear container: open the app, do today's lesson, tick it off, repeat. Reviewers generally praise the clean design and low-pressure pace. If you're starting from zero and respond well to a fixed program with an end date, Coursiv's structure does that job.

sections.heading: Where Learnova wins
sections.html: Breadth and checkpoints are where Learnova pulls ahead. Instead of one challenge, it breaks AI tools into a library of step-by-step courses with quizzes along the way and a hands-on playground to try things. It also offers a free basic tier, which makes it easier to evaluate before paying. If you want to browse a catalog and pick your own route through it, Learnova fits that shape better.

sections.heading: Pricing, honestly
sections.html:
This is where most of the frustration with both apps shows up in reviews, so read this part carefully.

Coursiv typically leads with a discounted introductory offer that then renews automatically as a recurring multi-week subscription. The intro price is not the ongoing price, track the renewal date and amount before you commit.

Learnova uses a more conventional tiered model: a free basic plan with limited access, plus premium subscriptions for the full catalog. Fairer on its face, but the same rule applies: check exactly what the free tier includes and what premium renews at.

Neither model is a scam; both are common in consumer apps. The pattern to avoid is subscribing on an intro price without knowing the renewal terms.

sections.heading: The third option: skip the course format entirely
sections.html:
Here's the uncomfortable question about both apps: do you actually finish course-style lessons? If guided lessons feel like homework (you start the challenge, fall behind by day 9, and quietly stop opening the app), the fix isn't a different course app. It's a different learning model.

Iro AI is built on active practice instead: game-like drills where you write real prompts, get instant feedback, keep a streak, and climb ranks, about five minutes a day, more Duolingo than curriculum. A free AI IQ test shows you where to start (no signup), the built-in Ask Iro coach explains anything you get stuck on by chat or voice, and Custom Paths generate a structured path on any topic you type, not just AI. It's free to start on iOS or in the browser, and Pro is one predictable price: $49.99 a year (about $4.17 a month) with a 7-day free trial.

The scale, since a drills app can read as the lighter option against two course catalogues when it is the reverse: 29 learning paths, 477 lessons and 3,000+ hands-on exercises across 24 exercise types, covering ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Grok, Copilot, prompting, agents and automation. The Prompt Lab grades prompts you write against a live model, and there are live duels, an Image Lab, and certificates you earn free and claim with Pro. Every path is open on the free tier.

For the deeper dives, see Iro AI vs Coursiv and Iro AI vs Learnova.

Third-party prices and ratings here are US figures at the time of writing and change without notice. Last reviewed August 2026.

sections.heading: How to choose
sections.html:
• You want a fixed, guided program with an end date → Coursiv.
  • You want a broader course catalog with a free tier to test → Learnova.
  • You learn by doing and want a daily habit that sticks → Iro AI.
  • Whatever you pick: read the renewal terms, and start with the free AI IQ test to see which skills you're actually missing.

faq.q: Is Coursiv or Learnova better for learning AI?
faq.a: They are closer than their ads suggest: both teach AI tools through short, guided, course-style lessons. Coursiv leans on a 28-day challenge format; Learnova is a tiered course library with quizzes and a practice playground. If you want structure and don't mind a subscription, either works. If you learn better by doing than by completing lessons, a practice-first app like Iro AI fits better.

faq.q: Which is cheaper, Coursiv or Learnova?
faq.a: It depends on renewal terms, which is where people get caught. Coursiv typically leads with a discounted introductory offer that auto-renews as a recurring multi-week subscription. Learnova uses a free basic tier plus premium subscriptions. Always check what the plan renews at before subscribing, to either, or to anything.

faq.q: Do Coursiv or Learnova have free versions?
faq.a: Learnova offers a free basic tier with limited access. Coursiv usually leads with a paid introductory offer rather than a free tier. Iro AI is free to start, and the free AI IQ test requires no signup at all.

faq.q: Is there a better alternative to both?
faq.a: If your complaint with course-style apps is that lessons feel like homework, Iro AI is the practice-first alternative: game-like drills with instant feedback, streaks and ranks, an AI coach you can talk to, and Custom Paths that generate a course on any topic you type. See Coursiv alternatives and Learnova alternatives for the full field.

faq.q: What should I check before subscribing to any AI learning app?
faq.a: Three things: what the free tier actually includes, what the paid plan renews at (and how often), and whether the teaching style makes you practice rather than just watch. Retention comes from active recall, not completed videos.
